tracks.title: Vector Engine
tracks.purpose: Establish the pulse and a short bass identity without sustained harmony.
tracks.hypothesis: A listener can retain the bass identity when the rim accents move.
tracks.invariant: Tempo, bass pitch cell, and four-beat kick remain stable.

tracks.title: Vacuum Bearings
tracks.purpose: Compare an established electro groove with sparse sustained harmony.
tracks.hypothesis: Atmosphere adds depth while the kick and bass remain easy to follow.
tracks.invariant: The bass rhythm and displaced hat accents remain recognizable through pad entrances.

tracks.title: Off Axis
tracks.purpose: Test ordered changes to one asymmetric bass cell within a broken electro rhythm.
tracks.hypothesis: A clear return makes phrase reversal easier to distinguish from changed accents.
tracks.invariant: The source pitch collection, tempo, and backbeat remain available as references.

tracks.title: Transfer Engine
tracks.purpose: Develop a complete electro form with pressure, recovery, harmonic movement, and a clear return.
tracks.hypothesis: A recurring bass cell can hold the long form together across changes in density and harmony.
tracks.invariant: The bass rhythm, root pulse, and recurring rim gesture connect the sections.

tracks.title: Identified Pulse
tracks.purpose: Keep an acid cell recognizable through one reversal and its return.
tracks.hypothesis: A stable pulse and repeated cell can reveal a change in phrase order without added harmony.
tracks.invariant: Bass pitch collection, kick clock, and source voice remain constant.

tracks.title: Second Horizon
tracks.purpose: Place independently spaced atmosphere around a steady returning acid figure.
tracks.hypothesis: Quiet seventh and ninth voicings can add depth without obscuring the recurring bass identity.
tracks.invariant: The acid rhythm and quarter-note kick persist while atmosphere and register change.

tracks.title: Order of Returns
tracks.purpose: Compare two orders of phrase transformation against one stable reference.
tracks.hypothesis: A listener can distinguish reverse-then-rotate from rotate-then-reverse after a clear reference phrase.
tracks.invariant: The source cell, pitch collection, voice, and kick clock persist across the two operation orders.

tracks.title: Seam Memory
tracks.purpose: Develop a long hypnotic form in which returning phrases and harmonic continuity survive changes in density.
tracks.hypothesis: Repeated returns can connect pressure and recovery without a constant increase in tempo or loudness.
tracks.invariant: The bass cell, source voice, drum pulse, and recurring interval relationships connect the long form.

tracks.title: Iron Intake
tracks.purpose: Establish a mechanical bass call and a short percussion response.
tracks.hypothesis: The bass call remains recognizable when the response enters after it.
tracks.invariant: The F pedal and first three bass attacks retain their identity.

tracks.title: After the Release
tracks.purpose: Keep the mechanical pulse while open harmony follows a pressure interval.
tracks.hypothesis: Sparse harmony can create recovery without losing the rhythmic anchor.
tracks.invariant: Root and fifth bass attacks retain the same rhythm across harmony changes.

tracks.title: Order of Force
tracks.purpose: Compare two orders of motif operations over a fixed mechanical pulse.
tracks.hypothesis: A repeated source phrase can make the two operation orders audible.
tracks.invariant: Both ordered variants retain the source pitch collection and event count.

tracks.title: Machinery of Return
tracks.purpose: Develop pressure, release, harmonic depth, and return within one long form.
tracks.hypothesis: An established bass rhythm can carry harmonic and texture changes through a long piece.
tracks.invariant: The root-fifth-octave bass cell and quarter-note anchor remain recognizable.

tracks.title: Paired Horizon
tracks.purpose: Keep a bass identity while its upper range changes stereo position.
tracks.hypothesis: A stable low anchor can support clear upper-bass motion without a new pitch sequence.
tracks.invariant: The bass phrase and central low-frequency anchor remain unchanged during the first return.

tracks.title: Quiet Curvature
tracks.purpose: Place irregular atmosphere above a steady pulse and a G pedal.
tracks.hypothesis: Independent texture timing can convey unfamiliar space without removing rhythmic confidence.
tracks.invariant: The G root, fifth, octave, and kick grid remain stable under the atmosphere.

tracks.title: Order Leaves a Trace
tracks.purpose: Compare ordered motif changes while the harmony retains its pitch classes.
tracks.hypothesis: Stable harmony can support recognition of different phrase orders and registers.
tracks.invariant: Every chord voicing contains pitch classes F, A-flat, C, and G.

tracks.title: The Surface Remembers
tracks.purpose: Develop a long passage through discovery, pressure, space, and harmonic return.
tracks.hypothesis: A retained bass cell and recurring harmonic shell can connect distant musical states.
tracks.invariant: The bass rhythm, root-fifth-octave relation, and harmonic cycle recur through contrasting sections.
